categories.main_business_segments: Popular, Inc. operates primarily through two main business segments: Banco Popular de Puerto Rico (BPPR), which provides retail, mortgage, and commercial banking services in Puerto Rico and the Caribbean, and Popular U.S., which offers similar services in the mainland United States, primarily in New York, New Jersey, and Florida. BPPR also includes specialized subsidiaries for auto and equipment leasing, investment banking, broker-dealer, and insurance services. The company also has a Corporate group supporting these segments.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: Popular relies on a mix of traditional and digital banking technologies, with significant dependence on EVERTEC, Inc. for core financial transaction processing, information technology, and security services. The company is investing in technology upgrades, including the acquisition of certain IT assets from EVERTEC, and operates online platforms for personal loans and co-branded credit cards. Credit risk is managed through comprehensive policies, quantitative modeling (including CECL for credit losses), and robust cybersecurity protocols.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Popular serves a broad range of customers, including retail consumers, small and medium-sized businesses, large commercial clients, and government entities. Its primary markets are Puerto Rico (where it holds the largest retail banking franchise), the U.S. mainland (notably New York, New Jersey, and Florida), and the U.S. and British Virgin Islands. Key products include commercial and industrial loans, mortgages, consumer loans, auto and equipment leases, and deposit services.
categories.geographic_coverage: The company’s operations are concentrated in Puerto Rico, which accounts for the majority of its assets, deposits, and revenues. It also operates in the mainland U.S. (New York, New Jersey, Florida), the U.S. Virgin Islands, and the British Virgin Islands. BPPR has the largest retail banking presence in Puerto Rico, while Popular U.S. maintains a regional presence in select U.S. metropolitan areas.
categories.supply_chain_position: Popular, Inc. operates as a downstream financial services provider, delivering end-user banking, lending, leasing, and insurance products directly to consumers, businesses, and government clients. It does not manufacture physical goods but acts as a service provider at the customer-facing end of the financial supply chain.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company’s strategic focus includes digital transformation, enhancing customer experience, expanding its U.S. equipment finance business, and strengthening risk management and cybersecurity. Recent initiatives include acquiring IT assets from EVERTEC to gain more control over digital channels, investing in talent development, and maintaining a strong capital position to support growth and shareholder returns. Innovation is also directed at developing new products and adapting to regulatory and technological changes.
categories.revenue_model: Popular generates revenue primarily through net interest income from lending activities (commercial, mortgage, consumer, and leasing), as well as non-interest income from service charges, fees, insurance, investment banking, and brokerage services. Additional revenue streams include mortgage banking, investment gains, and income from equity method investments. The company also earns fees from transaction processing and card services.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: In Puerto Rico, Popular faces competition from local commercial banks, credit unions, and a few large U.S. and foreign banks. In the U.S., it competes with community, regional, and national banks, many of which have greater resources. The company is the largest financial institution in Puerto Rico and ranks among the 50 largest U.S. bank holding companies, but it faces intense competition on pricing, technology, and service delivery.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: As of December 31, 2021, Popular had $75.1 billion in assets, $67.0 billion in deposits, and $6.0 billion in stockholders’ equity. Net income for 2021 was $934.9 million, up from $506.6 million in 2020, reflecting strong credit quality, higher net interest income, and improved non-interest income. The company is well-capitalized, with a Common Equity Tier 1 ratio of 17.42%, and has demonstrated solid growth in deposits and assets, particularly in Puerto Rico.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Popular’s value proposition centers on its leading market position in Puerto Rico, comprehensive suite of financial products, strong local brand, and commitment to customer service. The company differentiates itself through its extensive branch and ATM network, digital banking capabilities, and deep community ties. Its focus on innovation, risk management, and talent development further supports its competitive edge in both traditional and digital banking services.
